body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"siainbuletin"} -->
_Requested by **Sia** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2?thread=cmsg_01KaQfLZaF43QUMN3kcT7pW2ApjJf3fNB4nmVud6MqNpBi)_

**Before:** `M-x vulpea-hierarchy-graph` drew every parent/child link in the vault as one Graphviz SVG, which is too large for a big vault. `M-x vulpea-hierarchy-outline` showed the whole tree as Org headings.

**After:** Both commands first ask for a starting note and a depth. `vulpea-hierarchy-graph` opens an interactive graph in the browser: pan, zoom, and click a box to fold it. `vulpea-hierarchy-outline` shows native buttons: TAB or `[+]`/`[-]` expands a note on demand, RET visits it, and `c` picks a new start. The SVG export is kept as `vulpea-hierarchy-svg`. Notes at the last depth show how many children they hide.

**How:** One scope function walks the parent tree from the chosen note to the chosen depth. The browser page is generated HTML with the data embedded as JSON and no external assets. Titles are written with `textContent`, and the JSON escapes `<`, `>` and `&`. The button view reads the full tree from vulpea and expands only the branches you open. Tested on Emacs 29.3 with mock notes (scope, toggling, HTML output, and JavaScript syntax). Not yet run against the real vault database.

---

---

commit.message:
Scope vulpea hierarchy views and add a browser graph

Each command now asks for a starting note and a depth, so a large
vault can be explored one branch at a time.

- vulpea-hierarchy-graph opens an interactive graph in the browser:
  pan, zoom, click a box to fold it. The page is self-contained.
- vulpea-hierarchy-outline is a native buffer of buttons: TAB or
  [+]/[-] expands a note on demand, RET visits it, c re-scopes.
- vulpea-hierarchy-svg keeps the Graphviz SVG export.

Notes at the last depth show how many children they hide.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YKB9W9Svzsc4PYxBD8qL9Q

commit.message:
Read every parent link in a vulpea hierarchy metadata value

vulpea-note-meta-get-list with the link type only returns the first
link of each value, so `- parents :: [[id:a][A]], [[id:b][B]]' made the
note a child of A alone. The hierarchy now reads every link in each
value, and repeated `parents ::' lines still count one by one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Name hierarchy SVG exports by time, note and depth

vulpea-hierarchy-svg wrote one fixed file, so each export replaced the
last. Each export now goes to vulpea-hierarchy-svg-directory as
<creation date and time>-<note name>-<depth>.svg, for example
20261020T163734-ethics-2.svg, so diagrams never overwrite each other.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Add a vui outline for the vulpea hierarchy as a trial

vulpea-hierarchy-outline-vui builds the same scoped outline with vui:
each note is a component with its own expanded state, so [+] and [-]
re-render only that branch. The plain-button view becomes
vulpea-hierarchy-outline-native, so the two can be compared side by side.
vui is now a required package of the module.

commit.message:
Regenerate the sp-vulpea-hierarchy literate doc

The doc described the first version of the module. It now follows the
current code: a block per top-level form with a line-by-line explanation,
for the module and for its HTML page template. Tangling it rewrites both
files exactly as they are. Two double blank lines in the module became
single ones, so the blocks tangle back byte for byte.
